# Fork-maintained patches for rayward-external/litellm
#
# Upstream (BerriAI/litellm) uses ARG-variable FROM in Dockerfiles.
# Our fork pins literal image@sha256 digests so Scorecard/OpenSSF does not flag them.
# Upstream syncs may revert to ARG-only FROM; daily-patch-verify detects and re-pins.
#
# Format: <file> | <grep_pattern_that_proves_patch_is_present> | <human_description>

Dockerfile            | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM); this is the Dockerfile litellm-build-push.yml deploys (Scorecard PinnedDependenciesID)
backend/Dockerfile    | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
gateway/Dockerfile    | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
migrations/Dockerfile | FROM.*sha256:    | Digest-pinned base image (not ARG-variable FROM)
.github/workflows/codeql.yml        | timeout-minutes: 90                       | CodeQL analyze job timeout raised 30->90 min so python leg completes
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/log-injection                          | Exclude CWE-117 query: taint explosion from pervasive logging; same scaling class as py/clear-text-logging-sensitive-data
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | workflow_dispatch                          | Alert bridge for code-scanning triage; re-apply after -X theirs syncs that wipe .github/workflows/
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24         | Opt in to Node.js 24 runtime before GitHub's 2026-06-16 forced migration (upload-artifact@v4 is a Node 20 action)
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | list_secrets                               | mode=list_secrets: reads secret-scanning/alerts through the same security-events:write token scope, since the security-sweep's CCR token cannot call that API directly. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once the CCR/Claude GitHub App token gains secret-scanning-alert read scope directly.
.github/workflows/alert-bridge.yml  | REF_FILTER                                 | Optional `ref` input for mode=list. GitHub's /code-scanning/alerts endpoint without a ref filter does not surface alerts scoped only to a PR head/merge ref (found on 2026-08-04 triaging PR #182: the unfiltered list said 0 open alerts while the PR's own CodeQL check reported 1 new high alert); passing ref=refs/pull/<n>/merge (or refs/heads/<branch>) surfaces those. Also added per-alert file:line output to the list mode's step summary.
cookbook/livekit_agent_sdk/requirements.txt | json-repair>=0.60.1                  | Explicit pin forcing the livekit-agents[xai] transitive json-repair dependency past GHSA-xf7x-x43h-rpqh (unbounded CPU DoS via circular JSON-schema $ref). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once livekit-agents itself requires json-repair>=0.60.1.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | cookbook                                   | paths-ignore: cookbook/ and scripts/benchmark_* are example/benchmark code; excluded to prevent FP CodeQL alerts (py/reflective-xss #953, py/regex-injection #952, py/clear-text-storage #979 #980)
litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py   | re\.escape\(allowed_model_pattern\)        | is_model_allowed_by_pattern: re.escape() the wildcard pattern before building the match regex, closing py/regex-injection (#1024). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies the same escape fix.
litellm/proxy/guardrails/guardrail_hooks/litellm_content_filter/content_filter.py | resolved category file path escapes categories_dir | _load_categories: realpath/commonpath containment re-check on category_file_path immediately before use, closing py/path-injection (#1025) as defense-in-depth alongside the existing category_name regex validation. CodeQL (PR #182) flagged this same rule again on 2026-08-04: the containment check validated real_category_file_path but the subsequent os.path.exists()/_load_category_file() sinks still read the unsanitized category_file_path, so the taint path through the un-normalized variable was never actually closed. Both sinks now take real_category_file_path. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream applies an equivalent containment check.
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/stack-trace-exposure                    | Exclude CWE-209 query: tracebacks only reach loggers, ProxyException.to_dict() never serializes a traceback field, CodeQL cannot distinguish log sinks from HTTP response sinks
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization   | Exclude CWE-184 query: security-critical URL validation uses urlparse() tuple comparison; flagged startswith/endswith are non-security normalization (JWT heuristic, trailing-slash strip)
.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml    | py/request-without-cert-validation          | Exclude CWE-295 query: every httpx client resolves verify via get_ssl_verify()/get_ssl_configuration() (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/http_handler.py), defaulting to True and only disabled via explicit operator opt-in (SSL_VERIFY env var / litellm.ssl_verify / explicit param) for enterprise self-signed/internal-CA deployments; CodeQL cannot follow the dynamic default so it flags every call site
Dockerfile (ui-builder stage)        | FROM --platform=\$BUILDPLATFORM node:20\.18-alpine3\.20@sha256: | Literal digest pin for the ui-builder stage (was ARG-variable FROM \$UI_BUILD_IMAGE), closing PinnedDependencies #1009/#1020. Same pattern as the other stages in this file. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream pins this stage itself.

.github/dependabot.yml | package-ecosystem: "uv" | Fork-only dependabot config covering every ecosystem the fork's security sweep scans (github-actions, uv, pip for cookbook, npm for all 4 lockfile dirs, cargo for litellm-rust, gomod for terraform/provider and cookbook/gollem_go_agent_framework, docker for both Dockerfile locations); upstream has none. A 2026-07-25 security sweep found a second .github/dependabot.yaml file (added by an earlier sweep, commit 4ce563ba/#109) had silently split off the github-actions/docker ecosystems and the then-existing uv langchain ignore into a file GitHub does not read when dependabot.yml also exists — Dependabot was only ever running the entries in this .yml file, so those ecosystems and the ignore rule were dead since #109. Merged everything from the .yaml file into this one and deleted it. The langchain ignore itself was removed by the 2026-08-01 security sweep once the fork's pyproject.toml pins (langchain==1.3.9, langgraph>=1.2.4,<1.3.0) already satisfied the constraint the ignore was blocking Dependabot from proposing — leaving it in place would have suppressed every future langchain security bump, not just the resolved one. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove/merge if upstream ever ships its own dependabot.yml that a sync would otherwise clobber.
tests/proxy_admin_ui_tests/ui_unit_tests/package.json | "ws": "8.21.0" | ws override bumped 8.20.1->8.21.0, closing GHSA-96hv-2xvq-fx4p (memory exhaustion DoS from tiny fragments). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream's own override (if any) is already >=8.21.0.
litellm/proxy/management_endpoints/team_endpoints.py | Applied across all keys for this team\.\n    Example - update team TPM Limit | update_team's docstring documents mcp_rpm_limit (wording copied verbatim from new_team's existing line). UpdateTeamRequest gained the mcp_rpm_limit field upstream but update_team's docstring was never updated, so tests/documentation_tests/test_api_docs.py fails: it diffs a function's docstring against its request model's model_fields. Both the endpoint and the model are IDENTICAL to upstream, so this is upstream breakage, not a fork artifact — upstream's own CI misses it. NOTE the grep pattern is deliberately anchored on the following "Example - update team TPM Limit" line: new_team carries the same sentence, so matching the sentence alone would report this patch present even after a sync drops it. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream documents mcp_rpm_limit in update_team's docstring itself.
litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py | _translate_legacy_thinking_for_adaptive_model | Fork-only legacy thinking.enabled -> adaptive translation (infers an output_config.effort from the legacy budget_tokens, so pre-existing budget_tokens-based callers keep working on adaptive-thinking models) plus its _legacy_thinking_budget_to_effort/_coerce_optional_int helpers and the transform_request call site. Every -X theirs sync so far has silently dropped this (restored three times now: commit 343d3008, the 2026-07-12 sync, and the 2026-07-16 sync); it never conflicts textually with upstream's edits to the surrounding transform_request body, so git's 3-way merge just drops it instead of flagging a conflict. Signatures must be re-checked against upstream's current _is_adaptive_thinking_model/_validate_effort_for_model signatures each time (upstream has added a custom_llm_provider parameter to both since this was first written) — do not copy-paste the old diff verbatim. REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream ships equivalent legacy-thinking-to-adaptive translation itself.
litellm/proxy/response_api_endpoints/endpoints.py | @router\.websocket\("/v1/responses"\) | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): Responses API WebSocket mode is RE-ENABLED — the @router.websocket("/v1/responses") and @router.websocket("/responses") decorators on responses_websocket_endpoint, removed 2026-08-27 by #214 (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#645) because every non-Vertex leg failed after the upgrade, are restored now that the three root causes are fixed by the backports below (BerriAI/litellm#34253, #33101, #33463). tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_routes.py's guard was inverted from test_responses_api_does_not_register_websocket_mode to test_responses_api_registers_websocket_mode (now asserts the WebSocket route IS registered on both aliases) and tests/openai_endpoints_tests/test_responses_websocket_proxy_e2e.py's skip mark was dropped; ui/litellm-dashboard/src/lib/http/schema.d.ts had the two websocket operations restored. This row itself is not an ongoing patch (the decorators are vanilla upstream code) — it exists so a future sync that reintroduces #214's disabling logic gets caught by the guard test instead of silently redisabling the feature. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; delete this row if the decision to serve Responses WebSocket mode is reversed again.
litellm/responses/main.py | or api_key | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650, #645): _aresponses_websocket's resolved_api_key must stay `None` for a Bedrock/Vertex/SageMaker-style deployment, exactly like the HTTP path leaves litellm_params.api_key at `None` for those providers (litellm/main.py's bedrock dispatch never resolves an api_key at all: "boto3 reads keys from .env"). Upstream BerriAI/litellm#34253 (still OPEN) added `or api_key` ahead of a `litellm.api_key or litellm.openai_key or get_secret_str("OPENAI_API_KEY")` tail, which was necessary (it preserves an explicit caller-supplied key) but NOT sufficient: a Bedrock deployment with no api_key of its own still fell all the way through that tail to OPENAI_API_KEY, and base_aws_llm.py's get_request_headers treats ANY non-None api_key as an AWS bearer token, bypassing SigV4 and raising "Invalid API Key format: Must start with pre-defined prefix" (measured live against gateway.rayward.ai 2026-08-27, reproducing #645's original symptom). Fixed by dropping the cross-provider secret-store tail entirely: resolved_api_key is now `dynamic_api_key or api_key or litellm_params.api_key`, matching the HTTP path's litellm_params.api_key exactly, so each provider's own config/completion() branch resolves its own credentials or fallback (as OpenAI's validate_environment already does) instead of a generic OpenAI key racing in ahead of them. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestResponsesAPIWebSocketSupport::test_bedrock_websocket_does_not_leak_openai_key_as_bearer_token. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop when upstream BerriAI/litellm#34253 (or an equivalent fix) merges and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | call_kwargs\["proxy_server_request"\] = proxy_server_request | backport of upstream BerriAI/litellm#33101 (OPEN, "fix(responses): stop managed Responses WebSocket from leaking litellm_params into provider request body", rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler._update_proxy_request nested proxy_server_request under call_kwargs["litellm_params"], and litellm_params is not a Responses API request field, so strict providers (e.g. Anthropic) rejected the forwarded call with "litellm_params: Extra inputs are not permitted". Fixed by setting call_kwargs["proxy_server_request"] directly instead of nesting it under a synthesized litellm_params dict. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop when upstream BerriAI/litellm#33101 merges and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/responses/main.py | _build_responses_websocket_request_defaults | backport of upstream BerriAI/litellm#33463 (OPEN, "fix(responses): apply deployment defaults to websocket frames", rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): deployment-level defaults (reasoning effort, service_tier, extra_body provider params) passed to responses() were never threaded through to WebSocket response.create frames, so a WebSocket session silently dropped the caller's per-deployment configuration that the HTTP path honors. Adds _build_responses_websocket_request_defaults (litellm/responses/main.py) to collect those defaults, threads them as request_defaults through BaseLLMHTTPHandler.async_responses_websocket (litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py) and ResponsesWebSocketStreaming (litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py), which merges them into each response.create frame via the new _apply_request_defaults, filling in only keys the client did not already set. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop when upstream BerriAI/litellm#33463 merges and a sync absorbs it.
litellm/responses/main.py | custom_llm_provider=litellm_params.custom_llm_provider | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650): _aresponses_websocket's litellm.get_llm_provider(...) call ignored the router-resolved custom_llm_provider already sitting in kwargs and re-derived the provider from the bare model string alone. Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry and Vertex deployments deliberately configure a BARE litellm_params.model (no "azure/"/"azure_ai/"/"vertex_ai/" prefix) and rely entirely on the separate custom_llm_provider field for routing (gcp/modules/gateway_cloud_run/litellm.config.yaml.tmpl in llm-gateway-infra: "Keep model_name and litellm_params.model bare"). Re-deriving from "gpt-5.5" alone silently matched litellm's own OpenAI model-name heuristic, producing custom_llm_provider="openai" and OpenAIResponsesAPIConfig instead of Azure's — an OpenAI-shaped request against an Azure api_base, which Azure answered with `OpenAIException - 404 Resource not found` (measured live 2026-08-27, matching #650's Azure WS-bridge row). A bare "kimi-k2.6" (Azure AI Foundry) matches no heuristic at all, so the same re-derivation raised an uncaught `litellm.BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided` before a single WebSocket frame was ever sent — measured live as "no frames at all". Fixed by passing the already-resolved litellm_params.custom_llm_provider into get_llm_provider, mirroring the `if custom_llm_provider is None` gate aresponses()/responses() already use on the HTTP path. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestResponsesAPIWebSocketSupport::test_azure_websocket_honors_router_resolved_custom_llm_provider and ::test_azure_ai_foundry_websocket_does_not_crash_on_bare_model_name. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; this is a fork-local WS/HTTP parity fix — remove only if _aresponses_websocket is rewritten to resolve the provider a different way that still honors an already-known custom_llm_provider.
litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py | falling back to the managed bridge | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#650, #645): a native-WebSocket-capable provider (OpenAI, Azure) whose deployment does not actually expose a working wss:// Responses endpoint used to close the CLIENT's already-accepted WebSocket with code 1011 when the upstream handshake failed, because websockets 15.x raises InvalidStatus on a rejected handshake, not the deprecated InvalidStatusCode the old except clause caught, so it fell straight into the generic except-and-close branch (measured live against an Azure OpenAI deployment 2026-08-27: our gateway sends the client its 101, then the connection closes with code 1011, reason "server rejected WebSocket connection: HTTP 404", reproducing #645's "HTTP 404 during connection" row). Fixed by entering the native backend connection through an AsyncExitStack and catching the handshake step's failure separately: on ANY exception establishing the upstream socket, async_responses_websocket now instantiates ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler (the same HTTP-backed bridge every non-native provider, e.g. Fireworks and Vertex, already uses successfully) instead of closing the client connection, since the client has not received a single frame yet and bridging is strictly better. Guarded by tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestNativeWebSocketUrlConstruction::test_native_websocket_handshake_failure_falls_back_to_managed_bridge. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop once our Azure/OpenAI Cloud Run deployments genuinely expose a working wss:// Responses endpoint end-to-end and this fallback path is provably dead, or once upstream ships an equivalent fallback itself.
litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py | Realtime WebSocket mode is not supported on this gateway | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#646): Realtime WebSocket mode is DISABLED — realtime_websocket_endpoint closes with code 1008 BEFORE accept(), which uvicorn turns into a definitive HTTP 403 on the handshake (no 101 is ever sent). No realtime-capable model is served here (GET /v1/models: 37 models, none realtime; none declared in model-providers/*.tf), so upstream's accept-then-resolve handler gave clients a successful handshake and a socket that closed empty on the first frame (measured live 2026-08-27). The three @app.websocket decorators are deliberately KEPT: LiteLLMRoutes.openai_routes lists the realtime paths and upstream's test_routes_on_litellm_proxy asserts a bare /realtime route exists whenever any is listed (and /realtime/client_secrets, /calls, /transcription_sessions legitimately remain), so deleting them makes that test lie. A -X theirs sync drops the refusal block with NO conflict — re-apply it. GUARDED BY test_realtime_websocket_refuses_the_upgrade in tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_proxy_routes.py (asserts close code 1008 via TestClient); NEVER delete the guard instead. Four upstream tests in tests/test_litellm/proxy/realtime_endpoints/test_realtime_webrtc_endpoints.py drive the handler directly and assert the old accept-then-check behaviour; they carry the _REALTIME_WS_DISABLED skip mark and come back with the handler. REMOVAL CONDITION: delete the block and the skip mark as soon as a realtime-capable model is actually declared and served.

ruff-strict-budget.json | "C901": {\n    "limit": 319 | C901 (cyclomatic-complexity) ceiling bumped 316->319 during the 2026-07-19 upstream sync: scripts/ruff_strict_gate.py attributed 1 new violation to the sync diff itself (upstream commits merged in via -X theirs, not fork-authored code), and the fork's own pre-sync base (ed1ef0fe) was independently already 2 over the 316 cap (318 total) with nobody having caught it, since this gate only runs on pull_request and the base commit landed via a route that never exercised it directly. `make lint-budget-update` only ratchets a rule down when the branch's own count improves on it, so it could not reconcile an over-budget rule; the ceiling was bumped by hand to exactly the verified current total (319), giving zero extra headroom for future fork contributions. The repo's own budget-ratchet job (test-linting.yml) is explicitly documented as non-gating and exists precisely to surface a ceiling raise like this one as a review signal. litellm/proxy/common_utils/budget_window_headers.py | def format_budget_windows | feature (#481, reshaped #491): renders a key's CONCURRENT budget windows (1d/1w/1mo) into x-usage-budget. Broker keys set `budget_limits`, never top-level `max_budget`, so get_custom_headers read None -> "None" -> dropped by exclude_values, and the header NEVER shipped to an external caller. Carries `spent` alongside `limit` per window because x-usage-spend is LIFETIME and cannot be subtracted from a windowed cap (a fourth header was declined, owner 2026-08-02). #491 MOVED THE HEADER NAME: BUDGET_HEADER_NAME is now the fork-only `x-litellm-key-budget-windows`, NOT upstream's `x-litellm-key-max-budget`. Overloading the upstream name put two value types under it, which no reader can dispatch on — the fork's own gateway_cost.py did float(raw) and silently reported max_budget:None for every windowed key. NEUTRAL_BUDGET_HEADER_NAME ("x-usage-budget") is exported beside it so the guards can assert both halves. REMOVAL CONDITION: drop if upstream ever publishes per-window budgets itself. #491 FOLLOW-UP: format_budget_windows also COLLAPSES same-duration windows to the least-remaining one. The published format is a list keyed by window name and the customer-facing parser turns it into a dict, so two entries sharing a duration silently overwrite each other — and the later assignment wins, so the LOOSER cap survives and headroom is overstated. The sibling gateway shipped exactly this (1d;limit=1000 beside 1d;limit=5000 reported $4999.89 of headroom against a real $999.99 cap). Duplicates are not configured here today, but budget_limits is an iterated LIST not a mapping, so it is one config edit away. Do not simplify this back to a plain join.
litellm/proxy/auth/auth_checks.py | valid_token.budget_window_usage | feature (#481) — THE SOURCE. _virtual_key_multi_budget_check already reads every window's counter (it is the enforcement); this stashes what it read so the sync get_custom_headers can publish it without a second cache round-trip and without disagreeing with the numbers enforcement acted on. Losing this line leaves the formatter correct and the header empty — silent.
litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py | format_budget_windows(getattr | feature (#481, extended #491) — THE WIRING, tracked separately because losing it is silent and the formatter's own tests stay green. There are now TWO format_budget_windows call sites and they are not interchangeable: one fills the NEUTRAL `x-usage-budget` (for internal callers — the external allowlist drops it by design), the other fills the fork-only branded twin `x-litellm-key-budget-windows` that the external rename table reads. Losing either silently blinds exactly one audience. The same patch emits `x-usage-cost` / `x-usage-spend` at source so the documented contract works on the internal hostname too, and RESTORES upstream's `"x-litellm-key-max-budget": str(user_api_key_dict.max_budget)` — do not re-add the `or str(...)` overload a sync may suggest. NOTE the getattr: direct attribute access would raise AttributeError on EVERY request if the _types.py half is reverted by a sync, and breaks upstream tests that build MagicMock(spec=UserAPIKeyAuth) since pydantic v2 fields are invisible to a mock spec. Both were observed 2026-08-02. The wiring guards assert over the AST, not source text, because ruff format reflows these calls.

enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py | attribution = self._get_job_attribution(job) | 2026-08-21 sync merge corruption, round 3 (same recurring class as the 2026-08-09/2026-08-14/2026-08-15 entries above): upstream independently grew its own second job-claim layer this cycle (_claim_job_for_costing / _release_job_claim, called from inside _track_completed_batch_cost right before the spend-log write) alongside the fork's pre-existing layer (_claim_job / _release_job_claim / _finalize_job, called from check_batch_cost before _track_completed_batch_cost even runs). Both additions land in disjoint hunks, so the merge auto-applied both with no conflict, silently producing two claim layers stacked on the same row: the outer _claim_job flips batch_processed=True before the inner _claim_job_for_costing runs, so the inner claim's own compare-and-swap (where batch_processed=False) always finds 0 rows and _track_completed_batch_cost always returns None without ever calling async_success_handler -- batches stop being billed at all, and the row is left oscillating between claim and release every poll cycle. Also silently shadowed: Python keeps only the LAST definition of a duplicate method name, so the fork's fenced _release_job_claim(status="pricing") was shadowed by upstream's simpler unfenced one, meaning the release path stopped restoring status to "validating" too. Fixed by deleting upstream's newly-added _claim_job_for_costing method, its duplicate _release_job_claim definition, and the wrapping claim-check/try-release-on-exception it added around the async_success_handler call in _track_completed_batch_cost, restoring this file to byte-identical with the pre-sync commit for this whole region. REMOVAL CONDITION: none; regression fix. Separately, NOT fixed by this patch: upstream's new claim timing (claim right before the spend-log write, after the results fetch) exists specifically because claiming earlier -- which is what the fork's _claim_job still does, unchanged since before this sync -- flips batch_processed=True before the output file has been read, and the managed-files deletion guard treats batch_processed=True as "safe to delete," so a concurrent delete can remove the very output file an in-flight costing run is reading. This is a real, pre-existing gap in the fork's design (not introduced by this sync) that tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py::TestMultiPodBatchCostClaim (upstream's brand-new test class this cycle) catches; closing it requires moving the fork's claim point later while preserving its status="pricing" fencing, _reclaim_abandoned_pricing_claims sweep, and spend-already-recorded dedup marker, none of which upstream's simpler single-flag claim provides, so it is a deliberate follow-up, not part of this merge-corruption fix. REMOVAL CONDITION: track upstream's job-claim/locking layer maturity as in the 2026-08-09 entry above; additionally, reconcile the claim-timing gap once a deliberate redesign of the fork's claim point is scoped and reviewed.
litellm/proxy/prisma_migration.py | LITELLM_PRISMA_CLIENT_PREBAKED | Skips the standalone entrypoint's own runtime `prisma generate` when set. Genuine upstream breakage, confirmed present on a clean upstream checkout (Dockerfile, docker/Dockerfile.non_root, and prisma_migration.py are all byte-identical to upstream/litellm_internal_staging): upstream's own PR #37692 (merged into this fork by the 2026-08-21 sync) made the entrypoint return prisma generate's exit code by default instead of only logging it, turning a previously-silent failure into a hard one. prisma-python's generator.generate() unconditionally re-copies schema.prisma into the installed package and chmod's the copy even when the content already matches (prisma/generator/generator.py compares paths, not bytes), and shutil.copy's chmod step (copymode) requires owning the destination file -- something no arbitrary non-root runtime uid does for a file baked into the image at build time, no matter how the image's permissions are set up. The runtime images already bake the generated client from this same schema.prisma at build time, so re-running generate at container start is pure redundant work; skipping it removes the only place that redundant call is made (migrations/run.py's ProxyExtrasDBManager never calls it). REMOVAL CONDITION: remove once upstream either stops re-running `prisma generate` in this entrypoint for prebaked images, or prisma-python skips schema.prisma re-copy/chmod when the destination already matches.

enterprise/litellm_enterprise/proxy/common_utils/check_batch_cost.py | _claim_job called from _track_completed_batch_cost | 2026-08-22 resolution of the claim-timing gap left open by the 2026-08-21 entry above. The fork claimed a row before fetching its results, which flipped batch_processed=True while the output file was still being read. Two consequences, both real: the managed-files deletion guard (_get_batches_referencing_file filters batch_processed=False) stopped holding the output file, so a concurrent delete could remove the very file the in-flight costing was reading; and a worker killed mid-fetch left the batch marked processed, unbillable by any other pod until _reclaim_abandoned_pricing_claims swept it hours later. Moved the claim to where upstream's own claim sits, inside _track_completed_batch_cost immediately before logging_obj.async_success_handler, WITHOUT adopting upstream's simpler single-flag claim: the fork's status="pricing" fencing, _reclaim_abandoned_pricing_claims sweep, _mark_spend_recorded dedup marker and fenced _finalize_job are all retained, so the crash-re-billing and disable_spend_logs protections they provide are unchanged. Losing the compare-and-swap now costs only a duplicated results fetch (the winner bills exactly once) and is signalled to the caller by the CLAIM_LOST sentinel, distinct from the unroutable-row None. Callers that previously released a claim they held across the fetch no longer do so: a failed fetch never took a claim and leaves the row untouched outright, while a failed spend-log write releases inside _track_completed_batch_cost. tests/proxy_unit_tests/test_check_batch_cost.py::TestMultiPodBatchCostClaim (upstream's class) now passes; its journal and claim-call assertions were adapted to the fork's write shape (claim carries status="pricing"; the marker and fenced finalize are separate writes) while every behavioural assertion upstream makes is kept. REMOVAL CONDITION: track upstream's job-claim/locking layer maturity as in the 2026-08-09 entry above; the claim-timing divergence itself is now closed, so only the extra fencing/sweep/marker remain fork-only.

litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | requester_metadata: Final = call_kwargs.pop("metadata", None) | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#657, owner-approved 2026-08-28 as a governance fix, NOT a candidate for silent removal on sync): ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler._inject_credentials used to let a response.create frame's own top-level "metadata" object (a legal Responses API request field, e.g. a Codex session tag, forwarded verbatim by _build_base_call_kwargs) ride as a separate top-level kwarg alongside our user_api_key-carrying litellm_metadata. litellm.utils.function_setup only copies litellm_metadata into litellm_params["metadata"] when kwargs["metadata"] is falsy, so a truthy client metadata dict won that check and dropped user_api_key from litellm_params["metadata"]. This does NOT break DB spend logging: _PROXY_track_cost_callback resolves identity via get_litellm_metadata_from_kwargs (litellm/litellm_core_utils/core_helpers.py:280-297), which prefers litellm_params["litellm_metadata"] and is unaffected -- confirmed empirically. It DOES break cross-connection TPM/RPM enforcement: the active rate limiter, _PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler_v3 (litellm/proxy/hooks/parallel_request_limiter_v3.py:4157), reads standard_logging_object["metadata"]["user_api_key_hash"] to attribute a turn's tokens to the right counter, and that field is NOT protected by get_litellm_metadata_from_kwargs's merge -- so a colliding client metadata object silently dropped usage attribution from the counter the rate limiter reads (litellm_params["metadata"] is what standard_logging_object construction reads from -- verified deterministically with a real registered success callback, tests/test_litellm/responses/test_responses_websocket_all_providers.py::TestWebSocketProxyIdentityMetadataMerge; the further end-to-end claim that this alone makes a subsequent connection's pre_call_hook reject was attempted against the real _PROXY_MaxParallelRequestsHandler_v3 + real InternalUsageCache but could not be reproduced reliably -- its reservation/correction accounting behaved inconsistently across runs in ways not fully root-caused, so that specific claim is NOT asserted by a test; see TestWebSocketRateLimitEnforcementMechanism's docstring for the retraction and the static mechanism trace that does hold). Fixed by folding the caller's metadata under litellm_metadata (as "requester_metadata", mirroring add_litellm_data_to_request's own convention for the HTTP path) instead of leaving it as a colliding top-level kwarg. Scope: this fixes non-native providers only (anything routed through ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler -- Fireworks, Vertex, Bedrock-Mantle, etc.). Native providers (Azure, OpenAI) take a completely different code path (ResponsesWebSocketStreaming) with its own, separately-tracked usage-accounting gap (dispatches an entire connection's raw WS event list to the logging pipeline once at connection close instead of per-turn from a proper response object -- tracked as a follow-up on its own branch, not fixed here). REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; this is a fork-local WS/proxy-hook correctness fix protecting a proxy-internal contract (standard_logging_object metadata shape) that has no upstream equivalent to converge on. Remove only if ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler's per-turn call construction is redesigned in a way that no longer risks this collision.
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | RESPONSES_WS_TERMINAL_EVENT_CLASSES | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#657, owner-approved 2026-08-28 as a governance fix, NOT a candidate for silent removal on sync): ResponsesWebSocketStreaming (the NATIVE-provider WS bridge used when responses_api_provider_config.supports_native_websocket() is True -- Azure, OpenAI; a raw bidirectional proxy between client and upstream, distinct from ManagedResponsesWebSocketHandler) used to dispatch cost/usage exactly once per CONNECTION, in backend_to_client's finally: block at connection close, via _log_messages() calling self.logging_obj.dispatch_success_handlers(self.messages, ...) where self.messages is a raw Python list of stored WS event dicts. _get_assembled_streaming_response (litellm/litellm_core_utils/litellm_logging.py:3670-3693) has no branch for a bare list and returns None before any cost/usage is computed, so response_cost and total_tokens always came out 0/0.0 regardless of real usage. Confirmed against production: a live DB query against LiteLLM_SpendLogs for the 2026-08-28 04:00-04:45 UTC window found 11 _aresponses_websocket rows (one per WebSocket session, all model=gpt-5.6-sol/azure) against 200+ response.completed frames in the same window -- one row per SESSION, every row spend=0, total_tokens=prompt_tokens=completion_tokens=0, status='success' (written as zero, not skipped) -- exactly the "one row per connection, always zero" shape this bug predicts. Fixed by, as each response.completed/response.failed/response.incomplete frame is forwarded (inside backend_to_client's loop, not at connection close), parsing it into the correctly-typed ResponseCompletedEvent/ResponseFailedEvent/ResponseIncompleteEvent and dispatching it on a FRESH per-turn LiteLLMLoggingObj via _build_per_turn_logging_obj/_dispatch_turn_cost. This lands on _get_assembled_streaming_response's EXISTING correct branch for those three types (:3672-3673) -- no logging-layer change needed. A fresh logging_obj per turn is not optional: verified by running (not reading) that reusing one shared Logging(stream=True) instance across multiple dispatch_success_handlers calls silently drops every turn after the first, because the dedup guard model_call_details["has_dispatched_final_stream_success"] is keyed on the logging_obj instance. _log_messages() (the old close-time hook) no longer dispatches anything -- only sets model_call_details["messages"] for input-trace bookkeeping -- so the fix does not double-count against it. Row cardinality changes deliberately from one row per session to one row per turn; verified safe because SpendLogs' primary key (get_spend_logs_id, litellm/proxy/spend_tracking/spend_tracking_utils.py:190-201) prefers the response's own `id` over litellm_call_id, and every real provider response.completed event carries a genuinely distinct response id per turn (this fix also generates an independent fresh litellm_call_id per turn as a second source of uniqueness) -- see test_distinct_turns_get_distinct_request_ids. requester_ip_address (blank on every pre-fix WS spend row, per the same production query) is a side-effect improvement: the fresh per-turn metadata dict copies self.request_data["litellm_metadata"] verbatim, which add_litellm_data_to_request already populates with requester_ip_address at connection setup -- verified it threads through correctly (test_turn_cost_attributes_to_the_correct_key). Cost/usage read the ALREADY output-masked event string (same one forwarded to the client), so a PII-masked text block is never billed differently and masking never races ahead of or behind what gets costed (test_turn_cost_unaffected_by_output_pii_masking). SCOPE: this is forward-only. The 11+ zero-valued spend rows already written for past sessions are NOT backfilled or corrected by this change -- per-turn usage for those sessions is unrecoverable from the DB (it only ever existed in the forwarded WS frames, never persisted), and any historical correction is an owner decision touching production data, not something this patch attempts. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; this is a fork-local correctness fix for a code path (ResponsesWebSocketStreaming) with no upstream WS-mode cost-accounting equivalent to converge on. Remove only if this class's per-turn dispatch mechanism is redesigned in a way that no longer risks the once-per-connection/raw-list regression.
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py | self._pending_cost_tasks | gateway fix (rayward-internal/llm-gateway-infra#657, owner-approved 2026-08-28, part of the same native-path usage-accounting fix above -- NOT a candidate for silent removal on sync): the per-turn cost dispatch tasks _dispatch_turn_cost creates (asyncio.create_task(...)) were fire-and-forget -- no reference retained, and bidirectional_forward's finally: cancelled/awaited only the forward_task and closed backend_ws, never touching the cost tasks. Two distinct exposures, caught on review before landing: (1) asyncio's own documentation is explicit that the event loop holds only a WEAK reference to a bare create_task() result, so a task whose result is not retained anywhere can be garbage-collected mid-execution; (2) even with a strong reference, returning from bidirectional_forward without waiting on them risks losing an in-flight dispatch to instance teardown -- concretely, Cloud Run scaling the instance down after the connection ends (we run on Cloud Run and scale to zero) or a deploy/restart killing in-flight tasks; the realistic trigger is narrower than "the event loop stops" (uvicorn's loop keeps running other connections, so a pending task usually completes in practice), but not hypothetical, and it targets the worst possible turn: a client disconnecting right after its final response.completed leaves the LAST (often largest) turn of every session with the least time to flush. Fixed by retaining every created task in self._pending_cost_tasks (populated in _dispatch_turn_cost, discarded via add_done_callback) and draining it with a BOUNDED wait in a new _drain_pending_cost_tasks method, called from bidirectional_forward's finally: after forward_task is done (so no new tasks can still be added). The bound reuses LOGGING_WORKER_MAX_TIME_PER_COROUTINE (litellm/constants.py) -- the same env-overridable per-coroutine budget the SDK already applies to one logging dispatch via GLOBAL_LOGGING_WORKER -- rather than a new bespoke constant, and exists specifically so a hung callback (a stuck DB write, a slow webhook) can never wedge connection teardown. Also: _dispatch_turn_cost's JSON-parse-failure branch (a terminal frame that fails to even parse) now logs at WARNING instead of returning silently -- a terminal frame this code cannot parse is a silently unbilled turn, the exact failure class this whole issue is about, and it must be visible rather than repeating the original bug in a new place. Guarded by TestNativeWebSocketPerTurnCostAccounting::test_pending_cost_tasks_hold_strong_references, ::test_drain_waits_for_a_turn_dispatched_just_before_teardown (asserts with NO extra sleep after the drain call -- a test that slept afterward would pass whether or not the drain exists) and ::test_bidirectional_forward_drains_pending_cost_tasks_before_returning. REMOVAL CONDITION: none tied to an upstream PR; fork-local task-ownership fix for a fork-local per-turn dispatch mechanism with no upstream equivalent. Remove only if the per-turn dispatch is redesigned to no longer create ad hoc tasks (e.g. an awaited, ordered dispatch instead of fire-and-forget).
